can’t recommend Midlands Grizzly’s Dog Training enough!

Bruce our 5 month old Rottweiler is currently doing his off-lead training with Adam, and I’ve honestly never seen him so happy! He’s absolutely loving every session and responding so well to the training.

Adam is fantastic at what he does. He’s extremely knowledgeable, friendly and approachable, and it’s clear to see how passionate he is about his work and the dogs he trains.

It’s lovely to see Bruce enjoying himself so much whilst learning new skills and building his confidence. We’re really pleased with the progress he’s making and couldn’t recommend Adam highly enough!

Thanks Adam

We had our first consultation with Adam at Midland Grizzlys, followed by an hour of further training, and we couldn’t be happier with the experience.

Adam was extremely informative and took the time to explain dog behaviour, how to correct unwanted behaviours, and how to handle and control a dog properly on the lead. We have a strong Pocket Bully called Axl, who can be nervous around other dogs, cars and certain situations, so we were keen to learn how to manage this in the right way.

We were genuinely surprised by how well Axl responded during the session, especially being around at least 15 other dogs! The commands and techniques Adam taught us were really useful, and we left feeling much more confident and positive about the training ahead.

A big thank you to Adam for his knowledge, patience and guidance. We left the session happy, encouraged, and looking forward to the next one and seeing Axl continue to make positive progress. Highly recommend Midland Grizzlys to anyone looking for help with their dog! 🐾

We came to Adam for help with our Golden Retriever, as he simply wouldn’t listen. He had issues with resource guarding, was destroying everything, and both we and my elderly in-laws, who sometimes looked after him, were struggling to manage him. We were at our wits’ end, and he wasn’t even a year old at that point.

We first completed the Foundation Programme, which is literally about building the first layers of proper training, education and understanding of our dog, while also incorporating the socialisation aspect through working in a group.

We then moved on to the Off-Lead Programme, and we’re now two sessions in. Both sessions have been one-to-one with Adam, and this is where everything has really started to come together.

Adam told my husband and me that our dog would be going on off-lead walks with us by the second session. Honestly, I didn’t believe him!

Today, after just two sessions, our dog has had two off-lead walks. He listened brilliantly, and I actually enjoyed the walks so much that I can’t wait to take him out again tomorrow.

On top of that, I’ve managed to get our dog to drop something from his mouth without any issues or reactivity, and for the first time, I genuinely felt in control.

I honestly feel like I have a different dog, and I cannot thank Adam enough. His knowledge, expertise and willingness to help have already made a massive difference to our lives as dog owners.

I would highly recommend Adam to anyone struggling with their dog. The difference we’ve seen in such a short space of time has been incredible, and we’re so excited to see what else we can achieve with his guidance!

So this week we completed our final on leash training session with Adam and progressed to our first off lead .
Wow , having been impressed throughout the previous stage of Nova's training I was keen to start the next phase but had no idea what to expect.
I have to say that I would not have expected to have the experience that we did.
We do walk Nova off lead were and when we have felt safe to do so , usually around a quiet spot without to many people or wildlife to distract her but have never had the level of control or confidence to walk her along the road or through a busy park. Getting her to come back to us was normally on her terms
Im sure ypu get the picture.
Imagine my wife and I looking at each other when he proceeds to take us a walk round Aston and the park alongside the busy roads with Nova off lead.
To say we were nervous is the least of descriptions.
However ,our concerns were unfounded and we actually found ourselves enjoying a pleasant walk on a beautiful day in some of the best inner city scenery you'll ever find.
I won't go into what was taught to us today or what methods.
I will say that im seriously looking forward to the rest of the journey in Nova's training.
Adam is the real article when it comes to understanding a dogs behaviour and how to get the best out of them
He's also great at educating us humans to as we need the training to.
I'm not a wealthy man ,but I don't begrudge a penny spent.
In somethings you pay for what you get and having encountered other trainers
I am happy that my money is well spent and I wont be looking elsewhere.
Couldn't recommend more.

Adam has genuinely changed my life and the way I interact with my Boxer. Before training, he constantly pulled on the lead, struggled to listen, and his recall was almost non-existent around distractions. I’d completely lost trust and wouldn’t let him off lead.
From day one, Adam simplified everything and showed me that I was actually confusing my dog. The progress has been incredible—he now heels without pulling and listens to my commands.
I’ve only just started off-lead training and I’m amazed at how far we’ve come. Adam is a world-class trainer who makes everything easy to understand. I genuinely couldn’t recommend him enough!

I cannot recommend this trainer highly enough. The transformation in my dog has been remarkable.

Before the board and train, walking my dog was a constant source of stress. He would pull hard on the lead and continuously scan his surroundings for potential triggers. The moment he saw another dog, cat, stranger, fox or squirrel, he would become completely fixated, barking and lunging aggressively , and it felt as though all of his previous training disappeared. Also, when dogs or people came too close or approached us, managing his reactions was extremely difficult.

The progress since his training has been exceptional. He is now noticeably calmer, more relaxed and listens to me rather than constantly searching for his next trigger. He listens to commands consistently and, most importantly, responds to them the first time even in situations where he previously would have completely lost focus.

Adam didn’t simply train my dog, he educated us as owners too. We were taught how to properly handle him while out walking, how to recognise and manage his triggers, how to communicate with him effectively and how to reinforce his training consistently. We were also shown how to use the e-collar responsibly and appropriately, rather than simply relying on it. His off-lead training and recall were also worked on, and he now responds reliably when called, giving him more freedom while maintaining a strong connection with us.

My dog is calmer, happier and much more settled now. I no longer feel like I have to constantly scan the environment or prepare myself for the next reaction. I can finally enjoy taking my dog for a walk instead of worrying about what might happen.

This experience has given us more than improved obedience. It has given us confidence, understanding and a much better relationship with our dog. The trainer’s knowledge, patience, professionalism and ability to understand my dog’s behaviour have made a huge difference.

I am genuinely grateful for the work the trainer have done and for everything he has taught us along the way. If you have a reactive dog and feel overwhelmed or unsure of how to move forward, I would definitely recommend Adam!

I wish I had met Adam sooner! I am currently only on my second training session with my Husky x Rottweiler, Tyson, and the progress we have made in such a short time has been incredible.

Before attending these sessions, Tyson was extremely difficult to walk. He would take me for a walk rather than the other way around, constantly trying to bolt towards every dog he saw and rarely listening to me while on the lead.

From my very first assessment with Adam, I learnt so much about the correct use and purpose of a harness and flat collar, as well as how my own handling and walking technique was unintentionally encouraging Tyson’s behaviour. Once Adam explained what I was doing wrong and how to correct it, I made the necessary changes for both my sake and, more importantly, Tyson’s.

The difference has been remarkable. After only two sessions, I can now walk Tyson in a controlled heel, even when passing other dogs at close distances. Previously, I couldn’t get within 15 metres of another dog without Tyson lunging towards them, whereas now he is listening to me and remaining focused.

I genuinely cannot believe how much Tyson has improved in such a short space of time. Adam is extremely knowledgeable, professional and clearly knows exactly what he is doing. He explains things in a way that is easy to understand and gives you the confidence and knowledge to continue working with your dog outside of the sessions.

I would highly recommend Adam’s training sessions to anyone struggling with their dog’s behaviour or lead walking. The results speak for themselves, and I’m looking forward to continuing Tyson’s training and seeing how far we can go.

My partner and I being first time dog owners started our puppy training sessions with Adam in December last year. I wasn't able to attend all the sessions myself due to work commitments but the sessions I did attend I did not like Adam's conduct. He was very much a bully to both his clients and the dogs they brought. There was no option of using force free methods and no personalisation to the dogs needs. Adam couldn't even be bothered to learn your name or your dog's and only used your name if you were the name on the bank transfer, otherwise you were just shouted at with your dog's breed. Our pup was 12 weeks old when we started with Adam and we feel like we wasted so much of her prime learning time where she should've been met with patience and encouragement into the world around her instead of a noose around her neck.

As soon as the slip lead was off we had no response from her with her behaviours. The lessons she learnt on the slip only apply on the slip which means really she only knows to avoid pain rather than walk nicely and listen. On our last session with Adam I felt myself enraged by his conduct with a dog next to me- couple with a large bull mastiff who was a friendly but dopey thing who mainly just jumped on his owners and wasn't overly responsive even on a prong collar. Adam came to them and told them "I have seen him jump on you three to four times in this session and you've done nothing about it. You have elbows, you have knees, use them." Which is an extremely horrible and outdated way to treat a living creature with intellectual capacity and feeling. Over all I would not recommend and have warned other dog owners about this place.

If this is how the dog training branch behave I wouldn't trust their boarding branch with my dog for all the money in the world. BEWARE AND STAY AWAY!
